q: Peaty soils are one of the major soils of India. These are found in:
options: The areas of low rainfall with low leaching activity
The areas of high temperature and high rainfall with intense leaching
The areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation
The areas of semi-arid climate with salinity
key_text: The areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation
explanation: Peaty soils form in areas of heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation, where organic matter builds up. Semi-arid salinity describes saline soil and intense leaching describes laterite.

notes.text: - **Peaty / marshy:** areas of **heavy rainfall and high humidity with good vegetation**; organic matter 40–50%; black, heavy, highly acidic (NCERT: alkaline in places); Kottayam–Alappuzha, Sundarbans, coastal Odisha–TN, north Bihar, Almora. "Semi-arid with salinity" = saline soil.

exam: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
q: The arid & desert soil is found in the states/regions of:
explanation: Arid (desert) soils occur in north-west India – western Rajasthan, Kutch/Gujarat and adjoining Haryana-Punjab; Maharashtra has black soils.

notes.text: - **Arid / desert:** sandy, saline; poor in nitrogen and humus, **phosphate normal/high**; **calcium increases downward** (kankar) – **western Rajasthan soils are rich in calcium**.

q: Which one of the following bacteria present in the soil produces a peculiar smell if it rains on parched soil?
explanation: The earthy smell of rain on dry soil (petrichor) comes from geosmin made by soil Streptomyces (actinomycetes); Micrococcus and the other names do not make it.

explanation: Soil geography studies soil formation, types, fertility, distribution and use; hydrology, climatology and geomorphology deal with water, climate and landforms.

exam: APPSC Group-II Mains 2019 (18-07-2019)
q:
Match the following

I. Percolation

II. Permeability

III. Infiltration

IV. Saturated flow

A. Surface entry of water

B. Soil pores fully filled with water

C. Water movement through soil column

D. Ease of water movement
explanation: Percolation is water moving down through the soil column (C), permeability is the ease of movement (D), infiltration is entry at the surface (A) and saturated flow is when all pores are full (B): I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-B.

exam: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
q: Which of the following elements is depleted from soil most after crop is harvested?
explanation: Crops take up and remove large amounts of potassium (second only to nitrogen), far more than calcium, zinc or phosphorus, so potassium is the most depleted among the options.
